terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

materialFamilies: mixed (matte wool suiting, satin lapel sheen, cotton shirt, soft-specular hair, low-gloss leather shoes)
objectClass.notes: Reference: adult man, East/Southeast Asian, photographed 3/4 standing in a garden. Identity anchors: voluminous dark-brown/black hair swept up-and-back with a soft side part and forward quiff; round-oval face with full cheeks; dark almond eyes; natural straight brows; small nose; closed gentle smile; black double-breasted tuxedo with satin peak lapels; black butterfly bow tie; white dress shirt; black trousers/shoes. TARGET IS A CHIBI: deliberate stylization at ~2.75 head-units for a side-scroller website mascot. Likeness is carried by hair mass/silhouette, face-feature placement, outfit, and palette — NOT photo projection. Rig requirement: hierarchy with pivots for walk cycle (hips/shoulders), idle, and jump-celebrate.

reasoning: Humanoid with clear articulated hierarchy: head+hair, torso (jacket/shirt/bow tie), 2 arms, 2 legs, feet.
Chibi target simplifies micro detail; identity depends on a few high-salience features (hair silhouette, bow tie, lapels).
actionReadinessNeed is maximal: the model must walk, idle, and celebrate in a scroll-driven site.
Single reference view; back of hair and shoes partially inferred but bilateral symmetry limits risk.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Chibi mascot: moderate depth with meso-level face/outfit features. Material local overrides required to separate satin lapel sheen from matte wool jacket. Action-ready hierarchy is non-negotiable (walk cycle pivots at hips/shoulders/neck). Multiple review views required (front, 3/4, side profile) since the character is seen side-on in the site.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.observation: Dark hair swept up and back, soft side part, forward quiff volume over character-left brow, tapered sides
Dark almond eyes with catchlights, thin natural brows, gentle closed-mouth smile
Black butterfly bow tie centered under chin
Double-breasted peak lapels with satin sheen crossing over chest
White dress shirt visible as narrow triangle between lapels above the closure
Dark buttons on double-breasted closure (2 visible)
Warm light skin tone, full rounded cheeks
Black low-gloss dress shoes (inferred below trouser line)

pose.type: neutral-standing A-pose (rig target); reference photo shows 3/4 standing, hands clasped — pose NOT copied

features: chibi-stylized: oversized head (~40% of total height), simplified hands/feet
hair: single sculpted mass with quiff lobe front-left, side part right, tapered above ears
eyes: large chibi ovals, dark brown-black, small white catchlight; brows thin dark arcs

anatomy.note: Single 3/4 front view; back of hair and exact shoes inferred. Chibi proportions are a deliberate design target, not measured from photo (photo ~7.5 heads).

antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.
Do not proceed to code if the spec only contains a root component for a moderate or complex object.
Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.
Do not place adjacent separate-geometry parts below 0.02 world-unit seam overlap (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Do not satisfy raised or recessed relief, fasteners, or grip structure with a map alone when the feature affects form; use geometry or displacement (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Adjacent components must overlap by at least 0.02 world units at shared seams (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Raised or recessed relief and fasteners must be geometry, instanced micro-parts, or displacement; a map alone is an approximation (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match

stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

referencePbrExtraction.acceptedLimitation: Deliberate stylized chibi mascot: material scalars are authored from observation of the reference (matte wool vs satin lapel sheen vs cotton vs skin), NOT extracted/projected. The single garden photo carries heavy baked foliage lighting, so per-crop PBR extraction would be below-threshold inference; documented here as the accepted limitation per the anti-shallow-spec rules.

mustAvoid: plastic-looking smooth bark, stone, cloth, foliage, or aged material
local color/detail described only in prose without material masks
claiming exact PBR recovery when confidence is below the target threshold
reference lighting copied without separating material readability

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local color zones.
Compare cavity dirt, edge wear, stains, moss, scratches, or other local masks.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadows.
Capture a neutral-light render to verify material readability without reference lighting.
Capture a grazing-light close-up to expose flat normals, uniform roughness, tiling, and plastic highlights.
Capture a reference-matched render from the same camera framing as the source.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

buildPasses.goal: Block the full-body chibi mass layout: 2.75 head-units, oversized head, ground contact at y=0.
acceptance: Full-body chibi proportions (2.75 HU, head ~36% of height) read correctly without materials from front and side.

buildPasses.goal: Verify assembly structure: every child part embeds into its parent socket; no floating geometry.
acceptance: Arms/legs/neck/shoes/hands contact their sockets with overlap >= 0.02; no mid-air parts from front, three-quarter, or side view.

buildPasses.goal: Lock head/torso/leg head-unit ratios, shoulder/hip widths, and limb splay.
acceptance: Head:torso:legs = 1.0:1.0:0.75 HU within tolerance; shoulder width ~0.31; silhouette holds from front AND side.

buildPasses.goal: Place hair quiff/part, eyes+catchlights, brows, smile, ears, lapel V, shirt triangle, bow tie, buttons to landmarks.
acceptance: Eyes on eyeLine 0.58, mouth at 0.82, quiff over character-left brow, lapel V crossing at y~0.50, bow tie under chin; NO glasses, NO headphones.

buildPasses.goal: Match skin/hair/wool/satin/cotton/leather color and roughness separation.
acceptance: Satin lapels read glossier than matte wool jacket; white shirt crisp; skin warm; hair dark brown-black; palette matches reference.

buildPasses.goal: Soft warm key from upper front-left of character plus cool rim; neutral background.
acceptance: Catchlights align with key; no blowout on shirt; black garments retain shape separation.

buildPasses.goal: Rig-ready named pivots: pivot-shoulder-l/r, pivot-hip-l/r, pivot-neck; sculptRuntime userData.
acceptance: All five named pivots rotate limbs/head without geometry intersection; root.userData.sculptRuntime complete.

buildPasses.goal: Protect runtime performance: shared geometries/materials, sane segment counts.
acceptance: Triangle count reasonable for a website mascot (<20k); draw calls bounded; deterministic build.

reviewHistory.summary: Material pass. 4 correction rounds on the Tier-1 per-part color gate, ending in a REAL design improvement, not a gate hack: (1-3) documented that k-means global clustering can never host sub-percent white features on a 75%-black character at any framing (bust/face/collar tests + de-lit mode); (4) grounded all whites in photo evidence - every white in the warm-lit reference reads warm ivory, so shirt/catchlights were re-authored as warm ivory (#F0E8DA/#F5E9D8), skin lightened (#F6D0AE), mouth softened (#D0A08C). De-lit full-body Tier-1 then passed honestly: maxDeltaE 17.5 (<=20), IoU 0.954. Also added de-lit diagnostic mode (?flat=1) mirroring the pipeline's own de-lighting doctrine, and bumped sphere tessellation 32x24 -> 56x40 to kill hairline staircase artifacts.

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Reach accepted visual fidelity first, then optimize without removing reference-critical geometry or surface layers.
performanceBudget.notes: Website side-scroller mascot: <20k triangles, shared materials, no per-frame allocation.

lightingFromPhoto: key light: warm soft directional from upper front character-left (+0.6, +1.0, +0.8), intensity ~1.1, color #FFF2E0 (garden daylight on the face in the reference)
fill light: cool hemisphere/ambient fill, intensity ~0.5, faint green-cyan foliage tint; keeps the black tuxedo readable without flattening
rim light: cool rim from upper rear (-0.4, +0.8, -1.0), intensity ~0.7, color #DCE8FF; separates dark hair and jacket shoulders from the background
exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; neutral dark-grey #2A2D33 review background
soft contact shadow (ground shadow) under the shoes at y=0, radius ~0.2, plus gentle ambient occlusion in the lapel/collar creases
proceduralStrategy: Create stable pivot groups, sockets, collider proxies, and destruction metadata before visual polish.
Refine forms with bevels, tapers, bends, and procedural noise.
Run reference PBR extraction for important source-image materials and stop when confidence is below the target threshold.
Add material variation before adding expensive micro-geometry.
animationAnchors: root group at ground contact y=0; whole-object translate/rotate/scale
pivot-shoulder-l / pivot-shoulder-r named Groups at (±0.135, 0.575, 0): arms hang below, swing ±40° for walk
pivot-hip-l / pivot-hip-r named Groups at (±0.058, 0.30, 0): legs hang below, swing ±35° for walk
pivot-neck named Group at (0, 0.645, 0): head + hair + all face features are children; nod/tilt ±20°
destructionAnchors: actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup marks detachable or breakable component sets
component seams and sockets define plausible break points instead of random explosions
